target: Mae ganddo fo gar newydd.
english: He has a new car.
tip: 'He has' in the north is ‘mae ganddo fo’, a form of ‘gan’ (with) that changes by person: ‘Mae ganddo fo gar newydd’ = he has a new car.

target: Mae yfory'n waeth na heddiw.
english: Tomorrow is worse than today.
tip: ‘waeth’ is the irregular 'worse', from ‘drwg’, not ‘drygach’. ‘na’ means 'than': ‘waeth na heddiw’ = worse than today.

target: Caria 'mlaen gyda'r gwaith da.
english: Carry on with the good work.
tip: The ‘-a’ ending gives an informal command to one person: ‘caria’ means 'carry on' to someone you know well.

target: Credid bod y tŷ'n hen.
english: The house was believed to be old.
tip: The ‘-id’ ending forms a past with no stated doer: ‘credid’ means 'it was believed'. ‘Credid bod y tŷ'n hen’.

target: Bydda i'n anfon e-bost atat ti.
english: I'll send you an email.
tip: ‘bydda i'n’ is the future 'I will': ‘Bydda i'n anfon e-bost’ = I will send an email.

target: Mae gen i feddwl y byd ohoni.
english: I think the world of her.
tip: ‘meddwl y byd o’ is a set phrase for 'think the world of': ‘feddwl y byd ohoni’ = think the world of her.

target: Gwerthodd e'i hen gar y mis diwethaf.
english: He sold his old car last month.
tip: ‘hen’ goes before its noun and softens it: ‘car’ becomes ‘gar’ in ‘hen gar’ (old car). Most adjectives instead follow the noun.

target: Mae dychymyg yn bwysicach na gwybodaeth weithiau.
english: Imagination is sometimes more important than knowledge.
tip: Add ‘-ach’ for 'more': ‘pwysig’ becomes ‘bwysicach’ (more important). ‘na’ means 'than': ‘bwysicach na gwybodaeth’.

target: Dywedodd y meddyg y dylwn i orffwys mwy.
english: The doctor said I should rest more.
tip: ‘dylwn i’ means 'I should', used for obligation: ‘y dylwn i orffwys’ = that I should rest.

target: Dewisodd hi'r ffrog goch ar gyfer y briodas.
english: She chose the red dress for the wedding.
tip: An adjective after a feminine noun softens: ‘coch’ becomes ‘goch’ in ‘ffrog goch’ (red dress). Masculine nouns leave it alone.

target: Wrth i'r haul fachlud, trodd yr awyr yn oren.
english: As the sun set, the sky turned orange.
tip: ‘wrth i’ sets up 'as' for a background action: ‘Wrth i'r haul fachlud, trodd yr awyr’ = as the sun set, the sky turned.

target: Roedd y car wedi torri ar ganol y daith hir.
english: The car had broken down in the middle of the long journey.
tip: ‘wedi’ before a verb makes 'had done': ‘wedi torri’ = had broken. So ‘Roedd y car wedi torri’.

target: Pe bai mwy o amser, byddwn i'n darllen mwy o lyfrau.
english: If there were more time, I would read more books.
tip: ‘pe bai’ sets up an unreal 'if': ‘Pe bai mwy o amser, byddwn i'n darllen’ = if there were more time, I would read.

target: Yn hytrach na mynd allan yn y tywydd ofnadwy, penderfynais aros gartref a darllen.
english: Rather than going out in the terrible weather, I decided to stay home and read.
tip: ‘yn hytrach na’ means 'rather than' before a choice: ‘Yn hytrach na mynd allan’ = rather than going out.

target: Dyma'r llyfr mwyaf diddorol.
english: This is the most interesting book.
tip: ‘mwyaf’ means 'most' and comes before the adjective: ‘llyfr mwyaf diddorol’ = the most interesting book.

target: Mae'r bwyd yma'n llawer gwell.
english: The food here is far superior.
tip: ‘gwell’ is the irregular 'better', from ‘da’ (good), never ‘daach’. ‘llawer gwell’ means 'far better'.

target: Mae'r trên yn gyflymach na'r bws.
english: The train is faster than the bus.
tip: ‘na’ means 'than', but use ‘nag’ before a vowel: ‘yn gyflymach na'r bws’ (faster than the bus), ‘mwy nag ugain’ (more than twenty).

target: Dyna'r meddyg a driniodd fy mam.
english: That's the doctor who treated my mother.
tip: The linking ‘a’ means 'who' or 'that' and softens the verb: ‘triniodd’ becomes ‘driniodd’ in ‘a driniodd’ (who treated).

target: Mae llawer o ddefaid ar y bryniau.
english: There are many sheep on the hills.
tip: ‘o’ (of) triggers soft mutation, so ‘defaid’ becomes ‘ddefaid’: ‘llawer o ddefaid’ = many sheep.

target: Derbyniodd hi lythyr oddi wrth y cyngor.
english: She received a letter from the council.
tip: ‘oddi wrth’ means 'from' a person or source: ‘oddi wrth y cyngor’ = from the council. Use it, not ‘o’, for senders.

target: Cafodd Gwenllian y swydd ar ôl y cyfweliad.
english: Gwenllian got the job after the interview.
tip: ‘cafodd’ is the irregular past 'got' or 'received', from ‘cael’: ‘Cafodd Gwenllian y swydd’ = Gwenllian got the job.

target: Cysgodd y gath ar y soffa drwy'r dydd.
english: The cat slept on the sofa all day.
tip: ‘y’ (the) softens a feminine noun: ‘cath’ becomes ‘y gath’ (the cat). Masculine nouns stay unchanged after ‘y’.

target: Roeddwn i'n teimlo'n hapus pan glywais i'r newyddion.
english: I felt happy when I heard the news.
tip: ‘pan’ (when) triggers soft mutation on the verb: ‘clywais’ becomes ‘glywais’ in ‘pan glywais i’ = when I heard.

target: Roedd yr hen bont yn gul ac yn beryglus.
english: The old bridge was narrow and dangerous.
tip: The linking ‘yn’ softens the adjective after it: ‘cul’ becomes ‘gul’, giving ‘yn gul’ (narrow) and ‘yn beryglus’ (dangerous).

target: Dw i'n falch iawn o fy nheulu a'n treftadaeth.
english: I'm very proud of my family and our heritage.
tip: ‘fy’ (my) triggers nasal mutation: ‘teulu’ becomes ‘nheulu’ in ‘fy nheulu’ (my family).

target: Dw i newydd blannu blodau newydd yn yr ardd.
english: I have just planted new flowers in the garden.
tip: ‘newydd’ before a soft-mutated verb means 'have just done': ‘Dw i newydd blannu’ = I have just planted.

target: Er mai bach yw'r pentref, mae ganddo hanes cyfoethog.
english: Although the village is small, it has a rich history.
tip: ‘mai’ (southern ‘taw’) marks the emphasised word: ‘Dw i'n meddwl mai John sy'n iawn’ = I think it's John who's right.

target: Diddymwyd yr hen reolau.
english: The old rules were abolished.
tip: The ‘-wyd’ ending forms a past with no named doer: ‘diddymwyd’ means 'were abolished'.

target: Yr Wyddfa sy'n denu'r mwyaf o ymwelwyr.
english: It's Snowdon that attracts the most visitors.
tip: For emphasis, put the subject first with ‘sy'n’: ‘Yr Wyddfa sy'n denu’ = it's Snowdon that attracts.

target: Dw i'n dibynnu arnat ti bob dydd.
english: I depend on you every day.
tip: ‘ar’ changes shape by person: ‘arna i’ (on me), ‘arnat ti’ (on you), ‘arno fe’ (on him). Say ‘arnat ti’, never ‘ar ti’.
